3.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
3.text: "You've already agreed that you won't further tighten the EPA's restrictions. So I don't think I need to remind you how detrimental tighter restrictions would be to Gasom's operations."

7.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
7.text: "It could deter potential investors, thereby causing a ripple effect that could lead to job losses."

8.speaker: Narrator
8.text: The helicopter gradually reduced its speed, hovering for a moment before softly touching down on the helipad.

9.speaker: Player
9.text: "I'm committed to creating a favorable environment for businesses like Gasom. Your success translates to more jobs and prosperity for Sordland."

10.speaker: Player
10.text: "You're making it sound as if any change to the EPA would lead to an economic catastrophe. As the government, it's our duty to ensure energy security, not cater to private interests."

11.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
11.text: "I'm glad to hear that, Mr. President. Your support and understanding of our challenges are essential for us to thrive and contribute to Sordland's economy."

12.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
12.text: "Mr. President, I assure you that it's not about private interests. It's about allowing companies like Gasom to provide energy security, drive economic growth, and create jobs."

13.speaker: Player
13.text: "I hear your concerns, Mr. Alphonso. But we also have to consider Sordland's long-term energy security."

14.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
14.text: "Absolutely, Mr. President. Striking that balance is the key, and I believe we can achieve it together. Gasom is ready to be a part of the solution."

21.speaker: Narrator
21.text: A patchwork of verdant fields, sprawling forests, and untouched land stretched out beneath us.

28.speaker: Narrator
28.text: The further we moved from the mountains, the more rural the landscape became. Small clusters of wooden houses and farmers' huts began to appear, their rustic charm a stark contrast to the grey concrete of Narbel.

29.speaker: Narrator
29.text: We turned our attention to the stunning view below us.

30.speaker: Narrator
30.text: Serge leaned forward in his seat, his eyes tracing the path of the H-3 highway through the Sordish countryside.

31.speaker: Narrator
31.text: Serge's gaze traced the path of the still-in-progress L-1 railway. The ribbon of steel gleamed bright in the sun.

32.speaker: Narrator
32.text: We were approaching the outskirts of Lachaven. Serge leaned forward in his seat to get a better look at the city's skyline.

33.speaker: Serge Wolkner
33.text: "It's inspiring to see the highway construction from here, Mr. President."

34.speaker: Serge Wolkner
34.text: "What a marvel, Mr. President. I can't wait for the new railway to transform transportation in Sordland."

35.speaker: Serge Wolkner
35.text: "Lachaven... it's quite a sight, isn't it, Mr. President?"

42.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
42.text: "I must say, {BaseGameText.AlphonsoToPlayer}, that was quite the adventure we just had. Never a dull moment with you around, eh?"

43.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
43.text: "That was quite an unexpected twist back there, Mr. President. I'd hoped to celebrate our deal with a drink, not a protest."

44.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
44.text: "I have to admit, Mr. President, I didn't anticipate that our meeting would come to this particular end."

45.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
45.text: "Your driver did a great job escorting us out of there. He's a keeper."

46.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
46.text: "But it seems we made the right choice. Your driver did a terrific job escorting us out of there."

47.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
47.text: "Of course your driver had the right instincts. Escaping by helicopter was the safest choice for us both."

48.speaker: Player
48.text: "It was an adventure, wasn't it? And I agree, Serge's assistance was invaluable."

49.speaker: Player
49.text: "Yes, our safety matters most. But it's unfortunate that we had to leave under those circumstances."

50.speaker: Serge Wolkner
50.text: "Mr. Alphonso, it's an honor to meet you in person. I was trained by your former driver Nouman Fevon. He always spoke highly of you."

51.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
51.text: "I heard from Gasom security and the local police about some armed gang activity in the area a week ago. Better safe than sorry, right?"

52.speaker: Narrator
52.text: Alphonso had been quiet for most of the journey, but as we neared Lachaven, he finally broke his silence.

53.speaker: Player
53.text: "Yes, I'm glad we're safe. Although i can't help but wonder whether I should have spoken to those protesters."

54.speaker: Player
54.text: "I can always rely on Serge to get me out of a dangerous situation."

55.speaker: Player
55.text: "Yes, it was unfortunate how the situation unfolded. But a stroke of luck that you had a helicopter at the ready."

56.speaker: Player
56.text: "A shame about the protests, but to be honest, I'm not sure we were ever going to see eye to eye. The only thing we can agree on is that Serge was right."

57.speaker: Serge Wolkner
57.text: "Just doing my job, Mr. President. I'm glad we're all safe."

58.speaker: Serge Wolkner
58.text: "Truly unfortunate, sir. But safety always comes first."

60.speaker: Serge Wolkner
60.text: "That's what I'm here for, Mr. President."

61.speaker: Serge Wolkner
61.text: "I'm glad I could be of assistance, Mr. President. The important thing is that we're safe."

62.speaker: Serge Wolkner
62.text: "I'm just doing my job, Mr. President. Safety is top priority."

63.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
63.text: "It's just a pity we couldn't tap into the potential of our meeting before all this... chaos."

64.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
64.text: "The Gasom security and local police had been warning about potential armed gang activity in the area. It was best not to take any chances."

65.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
65.text: "Ah, Nouman! What a man he was. Always had a knack for lightening the mood, even in the direst of situations."

66.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
66.text: "Once we were stuck in a traffic jam for hours, and he started singing old Sordish folk songs right there in the car. He had the whole motorcade laughing."

67.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
67.text: "Ah, Nouman! What a man. He used to tell us the most outrageous stories to keep us entertained during long journeys."

68.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
68.text: "Once he convinced a junior aide that the presidential limo was haunted! The poor lad didn't set foot in it for a week."

69.speaker: Serge Wolkner
69.text: "Mr. Alphonso, I was trained by Nouman Fevon, your former driver. He spoke often of his time serving you."

70.speaker: Serge Wolkner
70.text: "Mr. Alphonso, I was trained by your former driver Nouman Fevon. He often mentioned the challenges of your presidency."

71.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
71.text: "Ah, Nouman. He was a real character. Always ready with a joke, even during the most serious of crises."

72.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
72.text: "His stories could get even the most stone-faced security agents chuckling. I hope he was a good mentor to you, Serge."

73.speaker: Player
73.text: "Serge, can you sing any Sordish folk songs to lighten the mood?"

74.speaker: Player
74.text: "Perhaps we should add singing ability to the job requirements for presidential drivers, eh Serge?"

75.speaker: Player
75.text: "Serge, I didn't know your job had such... unusual requirements."

76.speaker: Serge Wolkner
76.text: "I'm afraid I'm not much of a singer, Mr. President. But I know how to avoid traffic jams."

77.speaker: Serge Wolkner
77.text: "I don't know about that, Mr. President. I think driving skills should be first on the list."

78.speaker: Serge Wolkner
78.text: "Well, Mr. President, you never know what skills might come in handy. But I must admit, singing isn't my strong suit."

80.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
80.text: "I'm sure your driving skills are top-notch, Serge. But a sense of humor can be just as important."

81.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
81.text: "I'm sure you've got other hidden talents."

82.speaker: Player
82.text: "Do you have any stories for us, Serge?"

83.speaker: Player
83.text: "Serge, it seems like you have a tough act to follow."

84.speaker: Player
84.text: "Come to think of it, I do hear some strange noises in there sometimes."

85.speaker: Serge Wolkner
85.text: "I'm afraid I'm not much of a storyteller, Mr. President. I'd rather keep my focus on the road."

86.speaker: Serge Wolkner
86.text: "Indeed, Mr. President. Nouman was quite a character. I do my best to serve in my own way."

87.speaker: Serge Wolkner
87.text: "Whatever you hear, it's not the engine. I check up on it at least once a month to make sure it's running smoothly."

88.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
88.text: "A wise approach, Serge. We wouldn't want any nervous aides running around, would we?"

89.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
89.text: "And you're doing it very well, from the looks of it."

90.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
90.text: "Well done, Serge. I'll come to you the next time I need car advice."

91.speaker: Player
91.text: "Do you have any funny stories for us, Serge?"

92.speaker: Player
92.text: "He used humor to lighten a stressful situation. I see. Ever hear of humor, Serge?"

93.speaker: Player
93.text: "Serge, did learning from Nouman help you stay cool in a crisis?"

94.speaker: Serge Wolkner
94.text: "Mr. Rayne, Nouman had his style, and I have mine. I believe in maintaining professionalism at all times."

95.speaker: Serge Wolkner
95.text: "Of course, Mr. President. But I've found that focus and competence are more effective in managing stress."

96.speaker: Serge Wolkner
96.text: "Mr. President, Nouman's lessons were invaluable, but I have tried to develop my own style."

97.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
97.text: "I see, Serge. Different strokes for different folks."

98.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
98.text: "I'd pay good money to see this one in a car with Nouman. A straight man and a cut-up."

99.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
99.text: "It's important to forge your own path, Serge. I respect that."

100.speaker: Serge Wolkner
100.text: "The H-3 has the potential to connect the nation in a way we've never seen before. Your legacy will be etched into the very landscape of Sordland."

101.speaker: Serge Wolkner
101.text: "Seeing it from above is like witnessing history in the making."

102.speaker: Serge Wolkner
102.text: "Historical, yet modern. There's something special about this city."

103.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
103.text: "The H-3 highway... you know, {BaseGameText.AlphonsoToPlayer}, I was initially skeptical. But it could become a lifeline for our rural regions."

104.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
104.text: "Economically, the H-3 highway was a sound decision. It's a visible symbol of progress."

105.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
105.text: "I suppose the highway will have its benefits, but I can't help but think the funds could have been better allocated."

106.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
106.text: "Serge may be right. You could make a significant impact."

107.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
107.text: "Its impact on rural areas is still up for debate, however."

108.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
108.text: "To a project with a more immediate impact, perhaps."

109.speaker: Player
109.text: "The returns might not be immediate. But I truly think the highway will pay off in the long term."

110.speaker: Player
110.text: "Just wait until it's completed, Sordland will make progress in leaps and bounds."

111.speaker: Player
111.text: "Some of my ministers had concerns as well. But I believe the H-3 was a solid investment."

112.speaker: Player
112.text: "It's a symbol of Sordland's past as well as its future."

113.speaker: Player
113.text: "It shows the complexity of our nation."

114.speaker: Player
114.text: "There are some issues, but with your foundation, you're already making a difference."

115.speaker: Player
115.text: "Just wait until it's completed. Logistical operations in Sordland will never be the same again."

116.speaker: Player
116.text: "Yes, it's ambitious. But great change often requires bold decisions."

117.speaker: Player
117.text: "Your man Gus Manger made an especially convincing case for the railway's construction. I hope he was right."

118.speaker: Narrator
118.text: I peered out the window at the looming cityscape of Lachaven was quickly enlarging. The sea was visible in the distance, its blue surface dotted with cargo ships.

125.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
125.text: "An ambitious project, to be sure. But you'll need to ensure it doesn't become a white elephant."

126.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
126.text: "The L-1 railway... quite an investment. I hope it will not turn out to be a financial burden in the long run."

128.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
128.text: "The L-1 railway. Now that's a project I can stand behind."

129.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
129.text: "It's not only efficient, it's a statement. It shows that Sordland is ready for the future."

136.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
136.text: "What a city. It nearly brings me to tears every time I see it."

137.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
137.text: "Lachaven... it's a symbol of our nation, in both a good and bad way."

138.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
138.text: "But Lachaven has its issues, like any other city. We mustn't forget that."

139.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
139.text: "Wealth and poverty, side by side... it's a stark reminder of how much work people like us have left to do."

141.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
141.text: "It truly is the heart of our nation."

142.speaker: Serge Wolkner
142.text: "My apologies, gentlemen. I didn't mean to dominate the conversation."

143.speaker: Serge Wolkner
143.text: "It moves me to think about how many citizens' lives will change because of your project, Mr. President."

144.speaker: Serge Wolkner
144.text: "A revolutionary vision from a visionary president."

145.speaker: Serge Wolkner
145.text: "I can't imagine what it must be like to live here. Something exciting happening every day."

146.speaker: Player
146.text: "You prefer to keep things professional, right? Let's do that going forward."

147.speaker: Player
147.text: "Who needs Nouman's entertainment when we can listen to Serge Wolkner rhapsodizing about Sordland?"

148.speaker: Player
148.text: "No need to apologize, Serge. It's always a pleasure to listen to you."

149.speaker: Player
149.text: "That's quite all right. But I do have a few more things I'd like to bring up with Mr. Alphonso."

150.speaker: Serge Wolkner
150.text: "Understood, Mr. President. I'll make sure to keep that in mind."

151.speaker: Serge Wolkner
151.text: "It's true, Mr. President. I couldn't stay silent in the face of such a beautiful sight."

152.speaker: Serge Wolkner
152.text: "I appreciate you saying that, Mr. President. Sordland has always been my great love."

154.speaker: Narrator
154.text: As we began our descent towards the Blue Mansion, Alphonso shifted the conversation.

155.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
155.text: "We're approximately 25 minutes away from the Blue Mansion State Building, {BaseGameText.AlphonsoToPlayer}."

168.speaker: Player
168.text: "That sounds promising. These initiatives could significantly improve workers' lives."

169.speaker: Player
169.text: "That's an ambitious plan. I hope you can execute it."

179.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
179.text: "I can't thank you enough for Sordland's heavy investment in Gasom. Thanks to you, we'll be able to expand operations enough to meet both Sordish and global demand."

180.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
180.text: "Galmland, Qinal, and Anraka have all indicated their willingness to invest. If we were to eventually remove the EPA, the influx of foreign money could lead to significant profit for the state in the next round of investments."

181.speaker: Player
181.text: "It's a bold move, but it could indeed create an economic upswing. I'll consider raising the foreign ownership limit."

182.speaker: Player
182.text: "We must also consider the potential risks. Aren't you worried that increasing foreign ownership could lead to less control over our energy resources?"

183.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
183.text: "I'm glad to hear that, Mr. President. This could mark a new era of prosperity for Sordland."

184.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
184.text: "Maintaining control and ensuring energy security are indeed important."

185.speaker: Player
185.text: "Your argument is compelling, but it's a complex issue. I'll consider your recommendation."

186.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
186.text: "I appreciate your open-mindedness, Mr. President. All I ask is that we approach this with a clear vision of the economic potential it could unlock for Sordland."

187.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
187.text: "Mr. President, this strategic partnership with Rizia in Gasom is a promising step forward. It allows us to spread the initial risks and invites additional interest."
187.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Gasom_LargeSordlandInvestmentAlone"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Gasom_CoInvestmentRizia"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Relations_Ewald_PromiseNotHarsherEPA"] == true) == false)

188.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
188.text: "Of course they'd be a controversial partner, but as long as they hold a minority stake, we shouldn't face any significant issues. Qinal is also showing interest, by the way."

189.speaker: Player
189.text: "I understand your points, Mr. Alphonso, but we need to consider national security. Inviting multiple foreign powers into Sordland's energy sector could lead to problems down the line."

190.speaker: Player
190.text: "Mr. Alphonso, don't you think we're gambling a bit too much with the future of our energy sector? What if Rumburg decides to use their stake for political leverage?"

191.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
191.text: "National security is paramount, {BaseGameText.AlphonsoToPlayer}. But we also need to consider the economic potential."

192.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
192.text: "Rumburg's involvement could indeed be a double-edged sword. But we must remember that their stake would be a minority one."

193.speaker: Player
193.text: "This is a bold move. But it could indeed provide a much-needed boost to our economy."

194.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
194.text: "In my experience, fortune favors the bold. We're not only securing Gasom's future but also placing Sordland on the global energy map."

195.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
195.text: "I'm especially concerned now that it's become clear that Sordland is abandoning Gasom to its fate."
195.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Gasom_LargeSordlandInvestmentAlone"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Gasom_CoInvestmentRizia"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Relations_Ewald_PromiseNotHarsherEPA"] == true) == false)

196.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
196.text: "And that's not a prospect I relish. We're truly caught between a rock and a hard place."

197.speaker: Player
197.text: "I must say I'm disappointed that we are in this situation. As the chair of Gasom, you should have anticipated these challenges."

198.speaker: Player
198.text: "You're Gasom's chair. Can't you find a way  to save the company without risking our sovereignty?"

199.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
199.text: "Yes, the situation is far from ideal. But I assure you, we've done our best under the circumstances."

200.speaker: Player
200.text: "This conversation seems to revolve around accommodating foreign investors rather than serving Sordland. We shouldn't prioritize the interests of capitalists over our own citizens."

201.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
201.text: "Capital is a tool. Used properly, it can bring prosperity and create jobs."

204.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
204.text: "I worry that Sordland's unwillingness to invest in its own gas company might be perceived as a sign of weakness."

205.speaker: Player
205.text: "Our strength is not measured by how much we invest, but how wisely we use our resources."

206.speaker: Player
206.text: "We're showing that we can't be bought or influenced by money."

207.speaker: Player
207.text: "Strength can also mean resisting the urge to chase after every opportunity."

208.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
208.text: "Wise words, Mr. President, but if you truly believed them, you would have invested."

209.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
209.text: "A strong stance. But we must also remember that money is a tool, and it can be used to shape our destiny."

210.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
210.text: "Perhaps. We'll have to see how this approach pans out."

211.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
211.text: "Your government's large investment in Gasom will undoubtedly drive our economy forward and give us a stronger position in the global market."

212.speaker: Player
212.text: "Exactly. We're setting a strong foundation for future growth."

213.speaker: Player
213.text: "This is our chance to make Sordland a global leader in energy."

214.speaker: Player
214.text: "We're showing the world that Sordland is open for business."

215.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
215.text: "Indeed, {BaseGameText.AlphonsoToPlayer}. It's a move that will echo positively in our history."

216.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
216.text: "Absolutely, we're not just making an investment; we're making a statement."

217.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
217.text: "That's right, {BaseGameText.AlphonsoToPlayer}. It's a strong message, and the world is certainly watching."

218.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
218.text: "I'm sure that you agree it's important to maintain autonomy, even while co-investing with Rizia."

219.speaker: Player
219.text: "Agreed. We need to ensure our sovereignty isn't compromised."

220.speaker: Player
220.text: "I see this as an opportunity to learn and grow together with the Kingdom."

221.speaker: Player
221.text: "Our collaboration is a mere stepping stone to bigger and better opportunities."

222.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
222.text: "Exactly, {BaseGameText.AlphonsoToPlayer}. Maintaining control is crucial, even as we build stronger alliances."

223.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
223.text: "Indeed, we can definitely learn a lot from each other in this partnership."

224.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
224.text: "I share your optimism, Mr. President. The potential for growth is certainly exciting."

225.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
225.text: "I'm considering initiatives to provide private housing, health, and education support for our blue-collar workers."

226.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
226.text: "We need to ensure they're receiving competitive compensation."

227.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
227.text: "I'm considering supporting local charities in Narbel."

228.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
228.text: "Our company will do its best with the means it has."

229.speaker: Player
229.text: "I'm glad you're thinking along these lines. I expect more than mere consideration, though."

231.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
231.text: "I share your sentiment. It's time to turn these ideas into tangible actions."

232.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
232.text: "You're absolutely right. It's about making these plans a reality."

233.speaker: Player
233.text: "That's a step in the right direction. Fair wages are fundamental to worker satisfaction."

234.speaker: Player
234.text: "I'm glad to hear that. As long as this review isn't merely a token gesture."

235.speaker: Player
235.text: "That's long overdue. I hope to see substantial improvements in their remuneration."

236.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
236.text: "I agree. A satisfied workforce is a productive one."

237.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
237.text: "I assure you, this won't be just for show. We're committed to making real changes."

238.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
238.text: "I understand your concerns. We'll strive to make this review beneficial for our workers."

239.speaker: Player
239.text: "That's a positive direction. I hope to see Gasom leading the way in corporate responsibility."

240.speaker: Player
240.text: "Good thinking. But remember, sustainability is more than just philanthropy."

241.speaker: Player
241.text: "It's high time. I expect these considerations to translate into substantial changes."

242.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
242.text: "Thank you. We hope to set a good example for other Sordish corporations."

243.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
243.text: "Absolutely. We're looking at a comprehensive approach, beyond just charity."

244.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
244.text: "Of course, {BaseGameText.AlphonsoToPlayer}. You can count on that."

245.speaker: Player
245.text: "I appreciate your concern for Gasom's economic contribution, but it's crucial not to overlook the welfare of the workers and the community."

246.speaker: Player
246.text: "That's a narrow view, Alphonso. As Gasom grows, its social responsibilities should grow in tandem."

247.speaker: Player
247.text: "Maintaining the status quo is not enough. Gasom needs to be a part of the solution, not the problem."

248.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
248.text: "I assure you that we always strive to balance business growth with social responsibility. It's the Gasom way."

249.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
249.text: "A valid point. We will need to reassess our priorities as we move forward."

250.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
250.text: "I appreciate your input, {BaseGameText.AlphonsoToPlayer}. I'll take your thoughts into consideration as we plan for the future."

251.speaker: Narrator
251.text: He looked out the window and yawned.

252.speaker: Narrator
252.text: Alphonso scribbled something on his notepad and passed it to one of his assistants in the helicopter.

253.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
253.text: "Following our earlier conversation, I've been contemplating how Gasom can play a larger role in supporting our workers and the community."

254.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
254.text: "Based on our earlier discussion, I'm going to push for a review of our workers' salaries."

255.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
255.text: "In light of our discussion today, I've been thinking about how Gasom can implement sustainable practices and enhance our community engagement."
255.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_FreeHousingEducationHealthBenefits"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_IncreasedBlueCollarWages"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_LocalCharityDonation"] == true)

256.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
256.text: "As for Gasom itself, we need to focus on maintaining our current bottom line rather than stretching ourselves thin."
256.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_FreeHousingEducationHealthBenefits"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_IncreasedBlueCollarWages"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_LocalCharityDonation"] == true) == false)

257.speaker: Player
257.text: "As long as Gasom is doing well, I'm not concerned about how you choose to distribute your resources."

258.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
258.text: "I appreciate your trust in Gasom's management."

259.speaker: Player
259.text: "The financial situation of Gasom's employees is not my concern. They're paid for their work, aren't they?"

260.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
260.text: "Yes, they are. Our company has some of the country's best-paid engineering jobs."

261.speaker: Player
261.text: "As long as the workers are doing their jobs and Gasom is profitable, I see no reason to change anything."

262.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
262.text: "I appreciate your pragmatic approach. But investing in our workers' welfare can also lead to increased productivity and profitability."

263.speaker: Player
263.text: "Your ideas are commendable, but they're not my priority."

264.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
264.text: "I understand. But I do believe that more engagement with the community around us will have a positive impact on our productivity."

265.speaker: Narrator
265.text: Republic Avenue stretched directly beneath us, a grand boulevard lined with palm trees and decorated with sculptures. Even from this height, landmarks like the Evaria Gallery of Art, the Maroon Theatre, and the Lachaven Opera House were discernible.

266.speaker: Narrator
266.text: We were hovering over Lachaven now. The entire city was visible below us, its activity concentrated on its bustling port.

267.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
267.text: "One last thing before we land. I've been hearing noise about your administration making changes to the Energy Protection Act."

268.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
268.text: "You might remember that I struggled to repeal it during my term, and that said struggle was in vain. The Energy Protection Act of 1932 remains in force, and the restrictions on foreign ownership of energy companies in Sordland persist."

269.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
269.text: "The vote was 179 against the repeal to 71 in favor. The status quo prevailed, as it has to this day."

270.speaker: Player
270.text: "I understand why you sponsored the motion. But you of all people should understand the importance of protecting Sordland's crucial energy sector."

271.speaker: Player
271.text: "The defeat of the repeal was a setback for our plans to liberalize the economy. We must strategize and push for it in the next Assembly session."

272.speaker: Player
272.text: "I'm glad the repeal was defeated. We should not open our energy sector to foreign control. We must prioritize Sordland's sovereignty."

273.speaker: Player
273.text: "The defeat of the repeal wasn't surprising given the political climate. I'd rather focus my efforts elsewhere."

274.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
274.text: "Of course I do. But I also understand that the right amount of foreign investment could rejuvenate both our energy sector and our economy as a whole."

275.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
275.text: "I agree. It's clear that you'll need a different approach to win over the majority."

276.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
276.text: "I still believe that the repeal would have attracted much-needed foreign investment."

277.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
277.text: "We must be pragmatic and pick our battles. This is *the* battle to fight."

278.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
278.text: "I'm still mulling over the implications of your investment decision, by the way."

280.speaker: Narrator
280.text: I cast my gaze over the harbor teeming with ships and the distinctive buildings of downtown. Their Lespian-style architecture lent the skyline a flavor unlike anywhere else in Sordland.

281.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
281.text: "With that stage set, I believe an increase in the foreign ownership limit to 49% under the Energy Protection Act would attract considerable international investment."

282.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
282.text: "However, with the right regulatory framework, we can do both while still benefiting from foreign investment."

283.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
283.text: "Our foundation is strong, and our potential is limitless."

284.speaker: Player
284.text: "I agree, Mr. Alphonso. With the state on board, Gasom's future will be bright."

285.speaker: Player
285.text: "You still haven't convinced me. But consider Sordland's investment a vote of confidence for now."

286.speaker: Player
286.text: "Gasom's future certainly looks promising, but the decision about the EPA is a complicated one."

287.speaker: Player
287.text: "I'm not so sure, Mr. Alphonso. We mustn't become over-reliant on Gasom or overly susceptible to foreign influence."

288.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
288.text: "I understand your concerns, Mr. President. It's certainly a complex situation."

289.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
289.text: "Absolutely, Mr. President. Give it all the time you need."

292.speaker: Narrator
292.text: Suddenly, the former president's attention shifted as the pilot announced our landing over the intercom.

293.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
293.text: "That'll be it then, {BaseGameText.AlphonsoToPlayer}. I urge you to remain seated. These landings can be bumpy."

294.speaker: Serge Wolkner
294.text: "Thank you again for your assistance with the helicopter, Mr. Alphonso."

295.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
295.text: "Thank you for your fine company, Mr. Wolkner."

296.speaker: Narrator
296.text: The ground crew and Presidential Guard hurried to secure the landing site as Serge and I disembarked. Glancing back, I caught a final glimpse of Alphonso inside the helicopter.

297.speaker: Narrator
297.text: In a sudden rush of air and sound, the helicopter lifted off, headed towards the Gasom headquarters in the heart of Lachaven.

298.speaker: Narrator
298.text: I watched as it disappeared into the cityscape, swallowed by the luminous glow of the Lachaven skyline.

307.speaker: Narrator
307.text: A mutual nod of acknowledgement passed between us.

308.speaker: Player
308.text: "Good evening, Mr. Alphonso. It was a productive discussion."

310.speaker: Player
310.text: "It was a pleasure, Mr. Alphonso. Goodbye."

317.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
317.text: "Thank you for a stimulating discussion, {BaseGameText.AlphonsoToPlayer}. I have high hopes for Sordland's future, and for the continuation of the work we began during my presidency."

318.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
318.text: "Thank you for your time, Mr. President. I do hope that our discussion has given you some perspective."

319.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
319.text: "It was a pleasure discussing these matters with you, Mr. President."

320.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
320.text: "I didn't steer Gasom through tumultuous times and lead Sordland through a critical phase of its history only to watch my legacy disintegrate. I trust you understand the stakes."

321.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
321.text: "It's not easy to run a country while preserving one's legacy. I trust that you will take our conversation to heart as you steer Sordland into the future."

322.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
322.text: "Here's to a prosperous future for Sordland, Gasom, and the legacy we leave behind."

323.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
323.text: "I look forward to seeing how your decisions will shape our nation's future. We're fighting against the current, but I believe we can change the tide."

325.speaker: Player
325.text: "Not bumpy at all. I appreciate the lift."

326.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
326.text: "Their 15 percent stake is a fair deal. But I believe we could attract even larger international investments if the EPA is removed. Imagine the potential if Rumburg joined in."

327.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
327.text: "Don't forget that Rizia holds only a minority stake and we still have control over Gasom."

328.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
328.text: "In business, a certain level of risk is unavoidable. With the right safeguards, we can mitigate these risks."

329.speaker: Player
329.text: "Your confidence is reassuring. However, how can we ensure that Rumburg won't attempt to gain more influence over time?"

330.speaker: Player
330.text: "I share your views. However, I do worry about a potential backlash. The prospect of Rumburg buying a stake in our energy sector might not sit well with the public."

331.speaker: Player
331.text: "I am still concerned about the implications of letting foreign entities have a stake in our energy sector. Isn't there a way to boost our economy without compromising our sovereignty?"

332.speaker: Player
332.text: "The changes we make to the Energy Protection Act will have long-lasting implications for our nation's future. I can't decide this in a helicopter."

333.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
333.text: "Take all the time you need, {BaseGameText.AlphonsoToPlayer}. These are not decisions to be made lightly."

334.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
334.text: "As I've said before, it's a matter of striking the right balance."

335.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
335.text: "Public opinion is a vital factor, Mr. President. However, in my experience, people often resist change initially."

336.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
336.text: "That's a risk we'll have to manage. Regular reviews and stringent regulations can help keep their influence in check."

337.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
337.text: "Once they see the economic benefits, they usually come around. We have to be transparent and communicate our intentions clearly."

338.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
338.text: "Foreign investment can boost our economy, and as long as we ensure that our nation's interests are protected, I believe it's a risk worth taking."

339.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
339.text: "I trust your judgement in making the right call for our nation."

340.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
340.text: "Rizia's 20 percent investment will keep us afloat for a while, but it won't be enough. Any further tightening of the EPA restrictions will spell disaster for Gasom, possibly even leading to bankruptcy."

341.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
341.text: "The question now is, how do we move forward? And that's something we need to figure out together."

342.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
342.text: "We could consider other avenues like public-private partnerships or exploring new markets, but these options come with their own risks and uncertainties."

343.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
343.text: "Our challenge is to control it, not let it control us."

344.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
344.text: "It's a bitter pill to swallow, knowing that all of this could have been avoided."

345.speaker: Player
345.text: "Our resources are not infinite. We must prioritize, and sometimes, tough calls have to be made."

346.speaker: Player
346.text: "We have to remember the importance of keeping our energy sector secure. The idea of Rumburg gaining significant influence is worrisome."

347.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
347.text: "I understand the constraints you're under, Mr. President."

348.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
348.text: "I share your concerns about Rumburg, Mr. President."

349.speaker: Player
349.text: "While I sympathize with your position, the reality is that we had to make some hard choices."

350.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
350.text: "I'm not sure if I trust your judgement, Mr. President."

351.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
351.text: "I just hope we can navigate through this and find a solution that doesn't jeopardize Gasom or Sordland."

352.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
352.text: "But I believe that with careful consideration, we can find a way forward."

353.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
353.text: "I just hope that we can find a solution that ensures Gasom's survival without compromising Sordland's interests."

354.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
354.text: "On the other hand, loosening those restrictions too much will allow foreign entities like Rumburg to acquire a majority stake in Gasom."

355.speaker: Player
355.text: "Mr. Alphonso, I'm aware of the gravity of the situation. But we must not rush into decisions that could risk our sovereignty."

356.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
356.text: "Indeed, Mr. President. We must not be too hasty."

357.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
357.text: "It's a delicate situation, and the decisions we make now will have lasting implications for our nation's future."

358.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
358.text: "At the very least, I ask you to consider increasing the foreign investment cap to 49%. It might not be the perfect solution, but it could provide the lifeline Gasom needs."

359.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
359.text: "For old times' sake, let's work together to ensure Gasom doesn't become a casualty of our decisions."

360.speaker: Player
360.text: "It's a compromise that could save Gasom without compromising our sovereignty too much. I'll consider it."

361.speaker: Player
361.text: "Tightening the EPA laws further may be a necessary step for our future, even if it poses challenges for Gasom."

363.speaker: Narrator
363.text: The low rumble of the helicopter's engines reverberated through the cabin as we soared over the vast expanse of Nargis.

364.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
364.text: "Now that we've escaped an angry mob together, may I call you Anton?"

365.speaker: Player
365.text: "Of course, Ewald. You don't even need to ask."

366.speaker: Player
366.text: "I'd rather keep things on the professional level, if you don't mind."

372.speaker: Player
372.text: "It may not be perfect, but I'm proud to call it my hometown."

373.speaker: Serge Wolkner
373.text: "It must have been exciting to grow up here, Mr. President. Something new happening every day."

374.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
374.text: "Were Rumburg to get involved, they would be limited to a minority stake as well. I don't think it would pose a problem."

394.speaker: Player
394.text: "Its wealth disparities concern me. This place needs our help."
